scope: Eight bounded, individually sourced chronology strands. No automatic cross-strand alignment, no absolute AR date conversion and no assertions that a narrated legend is historical fact. The Thran-to-invasion strand uses the 2008 Wizards historical retrospective and does not decide the order between Old Phyrexia's decimation and Yawgmoth's destruction. The New Phyrexia strand describes early Mirrodin conquest, not post-March of the Machine politics. The Meditation Realm strand is Ugin's remembered early conflict, not a statement about the Realm's later state after Tarkir: Dragonstorm.

legacy_bridges.quote: the planeswalker Dyfed took Yawgmoth to Phyrexia shortly after its creator and master had died
legacy_bridges.note: The two ledger labels denote the same unnamed original Phyrexian master's death, without asserting that he was Yawgmoth.

legacy_bridges.quote: During the decline of the Thran Empire on Dominaria, the planeswalker Dyfed took Yawgmoth to Phyrexia
legacy_bridges.note: Both nodes describe Dyfed bringing Yawgmoth to Old Phyrexia in the same retrospective, not a separate later trip.

legacy_bridges.quote: The Thran were defeated, but not before the portal was closed, trapping Yawgmoth and the Phyrexians in their plane.
legacy_bridges.note: Both labels refer to the same closing of the Dominaria–Old Phyrexia portal during Thran defeat.

legacy_bridges.quote: The Thran were defeated, but not before the portal was closed
legacy_bridges.note: The same Thran defeat is described in both ledgers; its order relative to the portal is independently cited.

legacy_bridges.quote: The skyship Weatherlight and its crew traveled to Rath to rescue the ship's captain Sisay.
legacy_bridges.note: This is the same Sisay-rescue expedition, not every separate Weatherlight visit to Rath.

legacy_bridges.quote: Gerrard and the crew of the Weatherlight ended up in this plane after blindly flinging themselves from Rath.
legacy_bridges.note: Both refer to the crew's specific arrival on Mercadia after leaving Rath.

legacy_bridges.quote: Rath's purpose was fulfilled as it was laid over Dominaria like a sickly skin
legacy_bridges.note: This is the same Rathi overlay; the onset of invasion is a related, near-simultaneous but distinct event and is not bridged.

strands.title: Kamigawa — the Kami War and early Imperial administration
strands.limitation: Only stated within the Neon Dynasty guide's historical summary. The Imperials' founding is not automatically chained to the boundary breakdown without a direct before/after statement.

nodes.label: Konda imprisons a part of O-Kagachi
O-Kagachi retaliates and the Kami War begins
The imprisoned part escapes and becomes Kyodai
Kyodai and Michiko defeat Konda and O-Kagachi
O-Kagachi's death breaks the barrier between realms
Imperials are founded to aid Kyodai
Imperials expand into governance

edges.quote: Konda, Lord of Eiganjo, captured and imprisoned a part of O-Kagachi, the mightiest kami of Kamigawa. Enraged, O-Kagachi retaliated, plunging the mortal and spirit realms into a decades-long war.
edges.note: Retaliation follows the imprisonment; no absolute year.

edges.quote: The imprisoned part of O-Kagachi broke free and became a new kami named Kyodai.
edges.note: The fragment had to be imprisoned before it escaped.

edges.quote: The imprisoned part of O-Kagachi broke free and became a new kami named Kyodai. Kyodai partnered with Konda's daughter, Michiko, to defeat both O-Kagachi and Konda.
edges.note: The account presents Kyodai's emergence before the victory.

edges.quote: Kyodai partnered with Konda's daughter, Michiko, to defeat both O-Kagachi and Konda. The death of O-Kagachi caused the barrier between the two realms to break down
edges.note: The boundary rupture follows O-Kagachi's death in the narrated victory; does not order the individual defeats.

edges.quote: founded to help Kyodai manage the merging of the mortal and spirit realms. Over time, they expanded into government and rulership.
edges.note: Explicit 'Over time' after the institution's initial mission.

strands.title: Bloomburrow Valley — narrated local legend, not established universal history
strands.limitation: The guide tells the Order of the Holly Leaf and Calamities history in an in-world voice and calls the Order legendary. Order here is the order of the tradition's account, not proved historical sequence or an AR calendar.

nodes.label: Calamity Beasts dominate the ancient Valley tale
Animalfolk band together and shelter underground
Order of the Holly Leaf makes its legendary pact
The pact gives rise to mighty weaving in the tradition
War of Cinders is fought over two generations
Wildsear appears during the legendary conflict
Lily's Seed Flame drives back Wildsear
Unrestrained weaving causes destructive backlashes
Heroes' descendants seal the most powerful weaving

edges.quote: The oppressive heel of the Calamities imposed an unstable equality, a reason for those who could not contend with their power alone to band together.
edges.note: The storyteller describes animalfolk banding together in response to the Calamities.

edges.quote: Discontented to live their lives in the deep tunnels beneath Valley, a band was formed
edges.note: The narrated underground life precedes the formation of the Order.

edges.quote: However, their pact had another consequence. The land was now a wellspring of energy for them to draw from.
edges.note: The narrator says the magical transformation followed the pact.

edges.quote: Powerful as weaving was, the Calamity Beasts would not succumb to their terrible new powers. For two generations, battles raged throughout Valley.
edges.note: The account says weaving existed when two generations of battles began.

edges.quote: It was then that the greatest among the Calamities appeared: Wildsear
edges.note: The storyteller situates Wildsear's appearance during the war; 'then' does not prove the whole war ended first.

edges.quote: The animalfolk grew indulgent in the seasons after Lily has saved them. Weaving grew too powerful
edges.note: The excess weaving is explicitly after Lily's rescue in the traditional account.

edges.quote: In response to the chaos that weaving had wrought, the lineage of heroes chose to seal their most powerful knowledge away.
edges.note: The sealing follows and responds to the dangerous backlashes.

strands.title: Mirrodin to early New Phyrexia — corruption, conquest and Karn's restoration
strands.limitation: Only the official New Phyrexia plane overview's retrospective early-Mirrodin account. Its historical-present praetor politics are not a statement about present-day New Phyrexia after March of the Machine. This does not establish a complete war timeline, cross-plane synchrony or the precise order of Mirran defeat versus Venser's sacrifice.

nodes.label: Karn introduces Phyrexian oil to Mirrodin
Phyrexian oil transforms life beneath Mirrodin
Karn becomes the Father of Machines
Phyrexians begin the campaign to compleat Mirrodin
Mirrans fight against the invading Phyrexians
Mirran forces are overwhelmed in the early conquest
Venser sacrifices his life to restore Karn's sanity

edges.quote: which began the slow process of transforming the creatures it touched deep beneath the world's surface
edges.note: The overview directly links the brought oil to the ensuing transformation; no exact transmission date is supplied.

edges.quote: The slow spread soon became an active campaign to alter, or compleat, the world of Mirrodin.
edges.note: The gradual oil spread precedes the described active campaign; this does not order every individual infection.

edges.quote: The Mirrans fought many battles, but they soon were overwhelmed by the Phyrexian forces.
edges.note: The Mirrans' response is to the active Phyrexian campaign named immediately before this sentence; not a start date for every Mirran battle.

edges.quote: The Mirrans fought many battles, but they soon were overwhelmed by the Phyrexian forces.
edges.note: The overview distinguishes sustained resistance from its early defeat; this does not mean all Mirrans died or resistance permanently ended.

edges.quote: Even the Planeswalkers Koth, Elspeth, and Venser could not turn the tide, and Venser sacrificed his life to restore Karn to sanity.
edges.note: Planeswalker efforts to turn the tide precede the described sacrifice; no claim is made that all Mirran resistance ended before it.

edges.quote: Venser sacrificed his life to restore Karn to sanity
edges.note: Karn's prior corrupted leadership is the state restored from; the overview does not synchronize his ascent with each phase of Mirrodin's conquest.

strands.title: Duskmourn — the original House, Marina and the Ascension
strands.limitation: The guide's origin account does not specify an original plane name, AR date, post-2024 exit or present-day political status.

nodes.label: Valgavoth is bound within the original House
Marina encounters Valgavoth
Marina lures her bullies into the basement
The House's influence warps the neighborhood
Marina investigates the old House and discovers the demon
Marina demands that Valgavoth stop and threatens to burn the House
Valgavoth deceives Marina with apparent normality
The House ultimately consumes the whole plane

edges.quote: Trapped and unable to feed, the demon had sunk into hibernation and bided his time—until Marina came along and unwittingly loosened his shackles.
edges.note: The binding and hibernation precede Marina's involvement.

edges.quote: However, it was already too late. People around Marina began to meet sudden, unexplained, and terrifying ends. The neighborhood began to warp as well
edges.note: The neighborhood's distortion follows the basement victims in the guide's account.

edges.quote: But then, her parents vanished. Unable to deny it any longer, she delved into research
edges.note: Marina investigates once the spreading horrors and disappearances become undeniable.

edges.quote: Faced with the full truth at last of what she had done, Marina confronted the entity and demanded it stop.
edges.note: Her discovery precedes the confrontation.

edges.quote: With no other choice, the demon agreed to give her back the world as she remembered it.
edges.note: The false restoration follows Marina's ultimatum.

edges.quote: In reality, the house continued to expand. The horrors continued to increase, drowning all who lived within in terror. And the demon grew in power, until the entirety of the plane was swallowed up in the walls of Duskmourn.
edges.note: While Marina saw a false restoration, the House expanded into the Ascension.

strands.title: Muraganda — ancient collapse and early Grand Prix arrangements
strands.limitation: The guide reports ancient survivors' glyphs and the plane's later Grand Prix-era arrangements. It does not say the exact moon-shattering date relative to the collapse, that moon-strikes ended entirely, or when the Saurid Autocracy arose relative to the ancient survivor cultures.

nodes.label: Muraganda's ancient plane-spanning civilization discovers magic
Muraganda's first plane-spanning civilization collapses
Muraganda's moons shatter and their debris falls
Muraganda's moon-strikes abate over generations
Survivors form bands, tribes, and kingdoms over generations
Avishkari advance teams deploy ahead of the Muraganda race
Saurid Autocracy reaches agreements with Avishkari delegations
Avishkari crews discover limits of the Autocracy's treaties
Autocracy uses race agreements to extend its borders
Ghirapur Grand Prix race begins after its advance deployment

edges.quote: a plane-spanning civilization that ruled over Muraganda discovered magic and then collapsed
edges.note: The guide explicitly says 'then'; no absolute date or asserted cause of collapse.

edges.quote: The plane's moons shattered to pieces, and debris still falls onto the plane to this day.
edges.note: Moon debris had to begin falling before the strikes could abate; 'abated' does not mean ceased.

edges.quote: Muraganda changed over generations as the moon-strikes abated and survivors formed bands, tribes, and kingdoms.
edges.note: The source says 'as': these developments overlap and are not strictly sequential.

edges.quote: Advance teams from Avishkar were deployed to Muraganda a year before the beginning of the race.
edges.note: A relative one-year lead, not an in-universe absolute calendar date.

edges.quote: the race's security and maintenance teams have since discovered that the treaties their counterparts in diplomacy secured were only treaties signed with a map
edges.note: The discovery follows treaties; no universal agreement on behalf of other Muragandan cultures is implied.

edges.quote: From their easements and agreements, the Autocracy advanced their own borders along the race route
edges.note: The border expansion exploits the agreements; the source does not order it against Avishkari crews' discovery.

strands.title: Meditation Realm — Ugin's remembered early conflict with Bolas
strands.limitation: These are the historical events represented by Ugin's memory in the 2018 Chronicle of Bolas story, not independent absolute dates, a claim that Ugin permanently died, or a statement that the Realm remains intact or Bolas confined after later stories.

nodes.label: Ugin rests and meditates in the Meditation Realm
Nicol Bolas arrives in the Meditation Realm
Bolas attacks Ugin over the Meditation Realm waters
Ugin flees the Realm to Zendikar
Bolas pursues Ugin through several planes
Ugin returns to the Meditation Realm to await Bolas
Bolas strikes Ugin in the Meditation Realm
Ugin's fall triggers a cataclysm in the Realm
Bolas is thrown from the Realm to Madara
Ugin reconstitutes himself and departs the Realm

edges.quote: although he has rested here for long periods to contemplate mystery and eternity, Ugin cannot calm his turbulent thoughts now.
edges.note: The prior meditations precede the encounter in Ugin's memory.

edges.quote: Just before he hits the water, Nicol Bolas spreads his wings and rises. He shines as brightly as the sun, and ire is his color. With a howl on the wind and a searing blast of fire, he dives murderously toward his brother.
edges.note: The narrated arrival precedes the first attack.

edges.quote: Ugin takes the only path left open to him, even if it means Nicol will brand him a weakling and a coward for it. He walks out of the Meditation Realm
edges.note: The retreat follows Bolas's attack and Ugin's failed attempt to talk.

edges.quote: He walks out of the Meditation Realm and through the darkness to drop into storm-wracked Zendikar.
edges.note: The flight begins the subsequent pursuit across multiple planes.

edges.quote: Nicol will never stop pursuing him, not unless he thinks his twin is dead. He planeswalks back to the Meditation Realm, where he waits
edges.note: The deliberate return follows the extended pursuit in the remembered sequence.

edges.quote: In a burst of light, Nicol appears high in the lustrous sky. He dives, all teeth and claw.
edges.note: Bolas attacks after Ugin has returned and waited for him.

edges.quote: With a mighty splash, Ugin falls into the still waters. The impact resounds like thunder. Monstrous waves rise from the displacement
edges.note: The fall after the strike provokes the cataclysm; this does not certify permanent death.

edges.quote: Dragged by the sheer shocking force of the cataclysm, Bolas flares like a sun and vanishes, torn away to the plane of his birth
edges.note: The cataclysm displaces Bolas; his later status is outside this memory strand.

edges.quote: A pale sheet of liquid trickles up as out of nowhere, returning from the unseen and untouchable web of darkness.
edges.note: The following account shows the Realm refill and Ugin reform; the ontology and elapsed time remain uncertain.

strands.title: Thran decline to Yawgmoth's first Phyrexian invasion — 2008 Wizards retrospective
strands.limitation: This is the 2008 official retrospective, not a complete novel-era chronology or a current-status claim. The text independently describes Old Phyrexia's soul-bomb devastation and the Weatherlight's defeat of Yawgmoth, but supplies no strict BEFORE path between those two outcomes. Rath's overlay and the invasion's start are near-simultaneous, not two strictly separated events.

nodes.label: The unnamed creator and master of Old Phyrexia dies
Dyfed takes Yawgmoth to Old Phyrexia during Thran decline
Yawgmoth becomes master of Old Phyrexia
Yawgmoth's power grows in Old Phyrexia
The Thran grow horrified at Yawgmoth's actions
War erupts between the Thran and Phyrexian legions
The portal between Dominaria and Phyrexia is closed
The Thran Empire is defeated
Yawgmoth seeks to conquer Dominaria over millennia
Rath is designed as Phyrexia's invasion device
The Weatherlight crew travels to Rath to rescue Sisay
The Weatherlight crew escapes from Rath to Mercadia
Rath is laid over Dominaria
Phyrexia's first large invasion of Dominaria begins
Planeswalkers decimate Old Phyrexia using soul bombs
The Weatherlight crew uses the Legacy to destroy Yawgmoth

edges.quote: the planeswalker Dyfed took Yawgmoth to Phyrexia shortly after its creator and master had died
edges.note: The guide explicitly states 'shortly after'; neither creator identity nor an AR year is asserted.

edges.quote: Dyfed also created a planar portal between Dominaria and Phyrexia. Yawgmoth saw Phyrexia as a means of saving the Thran
edges.note: The account introduces Yawgmoth's arrival and purposes before saying he became the new master.

edges.quote: He became Phyrexia's new master. Fueled by Phyrexia's twisted ecology, Yawgmoth's megalomania and power grew.
edges.note: The official retrospective narrates the ascent before the subsequent growth of power.

edges.quote: Yawgmoth's megalomania and power grew. He came to believe that Phyrexia was the pinnacle of evolved life—that it was superior to life. The Thran became increasingly horrified by Yawgmoth's actions and their effects.
edges.note: The horror is described as a response to actions following his growing power; not a precise start date.

edges.quote: The Thran became increasingly horrified by Yawgmoth's actions and their effects. War erupted between the weakened Thran and Yawgmoth's Phyrexian legions.
edges.note: The retrospective introduces mounting horror before the outbreak of war.

edges.quote: War erupted between the weakened Thran and Yawgmoth's Phyrexian legions. The Thran were defeated, but not before the portal was closed
edges.note: The portal is closed during the conflict, before defeat; the exact battle is not specified.

edges.quote: The Thran were defeated, but not before the portal was closed, trapping Yawgmoth and the Phyrexians in their plane.
edges.note: The account explicitly puts closure before Thran defeat.

edges.quote: The Thran were defeated, but not before the portal was closed, trapping Yawgmoth and the Phyrexians in their plane. For millennia Yawgmoth sought a way to conquer Dominaria.
edges.note: The millennia-long search follows the historical trapping and Thran war.

edges.quote: For millennia Yawgmoth sought a way to conquer Dominaria. The eventual instrument of his invasion was the artificial plane of Rath
edges.note: The design emerges as the eventual means during a search begun earlier; no separate start/end of the search is inferred.

edges.quote: The eventual instrument of his invasion was the artificial plane of Rath, which was designed to lay over Dominaria
edges.note: Rath was designed for overlay before its purpose was realized; no invented construction date.

edges.quote: The skyship Weatherlight and its crew traveled to Rath to rescue the ship's captain Sisay. Later, when the Phyrexian aggression began in earnest, Rath's purpose was fulfilled as it was laid over Dominaria
edges.note: 'Later' explicitly places the Sisay-rescue journey before the overlay.

edges.quote: Gerrard and the crew of the Weatherlight ended up in this plane after blindly flinging themselves from Rath.
edges.note: The escape from Rath to Mercadia follows the crew's visit; its exact position versus the later overlay is not asserted.

edges.quote: The planar juxtaposition allowed a huge number of Phyrexians to enter Dominaria nearly instantaneously, beginning the Phyrexian invasion.
edges.note: The overlay enables an effectively simultaneous invasion onset; no strictly earlier-vs-later edge is added.

edges.quote: The invasion was narrowly thwarted by a coalition of planeswalkers and other heroes. A group of planeswalkers decimated Phyrexia itself using eldritch 'soul bombs,'
edges.note: The soul-bomb devastation is an outcome of resistance to the already commenced invasion; no ordering against Yawgmoth's defeat.

edges.quote: on Dominaria, the crew of the Weatherlight used the artifacts of the Legacy to destroy Yawgmoth himself.
edges.note: The Weatherlight's defeat of Yawgmoth is described as an outcome of the invasion; not ordered relative to the soul-bomb assault.

strands.title: Serra's Realm — Urza's refuge, the Phyrexian incursion and collapse
strands.limitation: The 2008 official summary recounts one historical sequence; it does not prove a complete angel/faction chronology, the timing of Radiant's administration against the final powerstone collapse, or any exact AR date.

nodes.label: Serra creates her artificial realm
Urza flees to Serra's Realm to escape Phyrexian pursuers
Serra and her angels heal Urza
Phyrexians find and attack Serra's Realm
Serra abandons the corrupted realm
Radiant assumes control after Serra's departure
Urza collapses the dying realm into a powerstone for the Weatherlight

edges.quote: This artificial plane was created by the planeswalker Serra to exemplify her love of peace and law.
edges.note: Creation necessarily precedes Urza entering the already existing realm; source gives no calendar year.

edges.quote: When Urza fled here to escape Phyrexian pursuers, Serra and her angels nursed him back to health.
edges.note: The nursing follows Urza's arrival.

edges.quote: Serra and her angels nursed him back to health. But the Phyrexians found the realm and attacked
edges.note: The summary places Phyrexian intrusion after Urza's convalescence; no precision beyond this sequence.

edges.quote: But the Phyrexians found the realm and attacked, tainting it with black mana. Serra abandoned the plane, heartbroken by its corruption.
edges.note: Serra's departure follows corruption caused by the attack.

edges.quote: One of her archangels, Radiant, assumed control of the plane in Serra's absence.
edges.note: Assumption of rule follows Serra's absence.

edges.quote: Without its creator, Serra's Realm was slowly collapsing. Urza, seeking a mana source intense enough to power the skyship Weatherlight, hastened its demise by forcibly collapsing the plane's energies into a powerstone
edges.note: The fatal powerstone extraction follows Serra's absence; the guide does not order it against the exact span of Radiant's rule.
